why-data-should-travel-with-proofs.text: Data travels with proofs so a terminal can check the claim it relies on against an independently accepted root. For an NFT, a ledger witness authenticates the output containing the application root; the terminal then checks the application proof against that root. External actions require their own authorization policy. Signatures establish endorsements, witnesses establish stated claims, and neither alone establishes completeness or freshness. Data and proofs may be retrieved separately when their bindings match.

components-and-chain-following.text: The diagram separates anchor infrastructure, shown in green, from provider infrastructure in blue. Both have nodes. An orange application builder consumes ledger history. Purple terminal verification receives roots and both levels of proofs. Shared code does not require a shared running process.

offload-computation-while-retaining-trus.text: An own anchor preserves independent roots while ledger archives and query capacity are outsourced. Institutional publications reduce local infrastructure under explicit institutional trust. CSMT-UTXO is the existing engine; its benchmarks and metrics start the cost assessment. The remaining comparison includes the node, commitment maintenance and additional archive and serving workloads.

data-and-trust-are-separate.text: Ledger providers and Lockness application services are both untrusted for correctness. An application builder may reconstruct state and generate proofs, but the terminal verifies every required claim against the root authenticated through the exact ledger output. Substitute roots, wrong applications, invalid proofs and missing evidence cannot become accepted facts. A builder checking its own inputs does not replace terminal verification.

proof-composition.text: The first diagram shows a chain-wide, application-independent ledger root authenticating a UTxO and datum. Interpreting that datum yields the application root. Application proofs authenticate values, which can carry further roots. Dashed links indicate optional nesting, not an automatic proof of descendants. CSMT-UTXO commits to the live UTxO set. The sequence then shows a terminal verifying an NFT output, requesting a proof for that verified application root, and checking the builder result. Ledger proofs concern present validity and stay off-chain; application proofs support future validation in redeemers. Every chain link must bind the expected identity, encoding and claim.

service-boundary.text: The ledger understands ledger structure but not application-specific meaning. It preserves transaction CBOR and resolves required references. Some responses are untrusted reconstruction material; other responses establish explicit claims through proofs.

decisions.text: The design reuses generic chain-following capabilities instead of creating an indexer per application. Independent trust remains separate from data provision, and clients may delegate proof construction without delegating verification.
